table.title: العربية · المنتجات
table.md:
| المنتج | السعر | المخزون | الوصف |
|---|---|---|---|
| حاسوب محمول | 3,200 ر.س | 14 | جهاز خفيف الوزن مع بطارية تدوم حتى اثنتي عشرة ساعة وشاشة عالية الدقة. |
| سماعات لاسلكية | 450 ر.س | 87 | عزل نشط للضوضاء. |
| شاشة 27 بوصة | 1,150 ر.س | 23 | دقة 4K مع دعم كامل لنطاق الألوان الواسع، مناسبة لأعمال التصميم والتحرير. |
| لوحة مفاتيح | 280 ر.س | 0 | غير متوفر حاليًا |

understanding.purpose: Arabic-language product inventory table for identifying each product, comparing price and stock, and reading a short description.
understanding.reading: Right-to-left: the eye lands on the product name first, then scans the compact price and stock columns for comparison, then reads the description as secondary detail; each row should read as one product record.
groups: col 1 (المنتج) is the row-label/identifier column and belongs on the right
col 2 (السعر) and col 3 (المخزون) form the numeric comparison group and should stay compact and adjacent
col 4 (الوصف) is free-text secondary content and can take the remaining width
keep_intact: price numerals and currency unit (e.g. 3,200 ر.س)
product names where possible, especially model numbers such as 27 and 4K
may_wrap: product names at spaces in narrower designs
currency unit only if a price column is deliberately compressed, never split the numeral

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Same price fix (91px, currency on one line) but also restore col 1 to 118px, the width at which product names — including 'شاشة 27 بوصة' and the 4K model — read on one line. This makes every row start with an intact identifier and a single-line price, i.e. two clean, scannable columns; الوصف drops to 156px (135px text) and will take three to four lines, so the table gets slightly taller but each row reads as one unambiguous product record rather than a stack of wrapped fragments.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Keep the r2B logic (product on one line, numeric columns at their one-line minimums) but give the product column 4px of slack above the 118px threshold so Arabic names no longer press against the cell edge; description drops from 156 to 152px, which at 131px of text still renders the long entries in 4 lines, so nothing gets taller.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Hold the product at its proven 118px one-line width and instead give the numeric pair matched breathing room (96 and 78) so price and stock read as one coherent comparison block with equal internal margins; the description takes the remainder at 147px (126px text), which still fits the long entries in 4 lines, so the visual gain costs no height.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Widen السعر from 66 to 91px so '3,200 ر.س', '1,150 ر.س', '450 ر.س' and '280 ر.س' each sit on one line — the numerals then form a true comparable column and short rows (سماعات, لوحة مفاتيح) can collapse to a single line height. The 25px comes out of الوصف (187→162), which costs at most one extra line in the longest descriptions; that is a fair trade because the description is secondary detail, while a broken price damages the table's main comparison job. col 1 stays at 112 (names wrap at spaces, no mid-word splits) and المخزون stays at its 74px minimum.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: A deliberate test of the opposite trade: accept a 2-line wrap on the two-word product names (112px, 91px text) in exchange for pushing the description to 162px. If the long descriptions still render at 4 lines, r2B/r3A is confirmed as the correct allocation; if any drop to 3 lines, the height saved may justify the split names. Keep this only if the render shows a row actually getting shorter.

bad.name: r1A
bad.note: Keep product at 118px so every product name stays on one line. Compress price to 66px: enough for the numeral 3,200 but not the currency, so ر.س wraps to a second line. Give the recovered 25px to description (181px, 160px text) so long descriptions fit 3 lines. Stock stays at its 74px header minimum. Tradeoff: price cells become two-line, but amounts remain aligned and the currency is constant, so amount comparison still works.
bad.why: Price column 66px breaks "3,200 ر.س" into number and currency on separate lines, so the price column can no longer be scanned as a single unit; the 181px description still needs 4 lines, so the extra width buys nothing and the table grows to 368px.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Same price-stack idea, but shift 6px from product to description. Product text becomes 91px, keeping shorter names such as شاشة 27 بوصة and لوحة مفاتيح on one line while the two longest names wrap. Description gets 166px of text for a comfortable 3-line measure. Row heights are still governed by description and price, so the partial product wrapping does not add height.
bad.why: Same price fault (66px splits number from ر.س) plus a 112px product column that wraps names like "سماعات لاسلكية" and "لوحة مفاتيح" onto two lines; the 187px description does not shorten, so the surplus is misallocated.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: A different allocation: accept two-line product names (already happening at 112px, and they break cleanly at spaces) in order to hand the freed width to the description. Price still gets its 91px one-line width so the numeric group stays intact and short rows stay short; الوصف rises to 174px (153px text), cutting the longest description back toward three lines and keeping total height near r1B while fixing the price fragmentation. This tests whether the identifier column is better sacrificed than the description, given that names are two short words and descriptions are long sentences.
bad.why: Product column at 100px starves the row-identity column (names wrap to two lines) to feed a 174px description that still runs 4 lines — the identity column is squeezed for no benefit.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: Plausible-looking but faulty: the 90px product column forces every product name onto 2–3 lines, the 70px price column splits the number from the currency, and the 209px description column wastes width because its longest lines still need 4 lines — surplus width goes to the one column that cannot use it while the two columns a reader scans first are cramped.
bad.why: Plausible-looking but faulty: the 90px product column forces every product name onto 2–3 lines, the 70px price column splits the number from the currency, and the 209px description column wastes width because its longest lines still need 4 lines — surplus width goes to the one column that cannot use it while the two columns a reader scans first are cramped.

rationale: In an RTL product table the right-hand المنتج column is the row's identity and السعر is the primary comparison column, so both must hold one line: product needs 118px (97px text) and price needs 91px (70px text, i.e. "3,200 ر.س" intact). المخزون is a fixed two-digit quantity that needs only 74px (53px text). r2B allocates exactly those one-line minima and hands the remaining 156px to الوصف, which is the only column whose content is prose and can absorb wrapping; it is also the shortest valid solution at 322px with no mid-word splits.

general: Fund each column to its natural one-line width before granting surplus to any wrapping column; a column that cannot hold its atomic unit (number + currency, name) becomes ragged and hard to compare.
Identity and comparison columns (names, prices) should not wrap; prose/description columns should absorb leftover width because their line count changes slowly with width.
Width beyond the one-line threshold frequently buys nothing: الوصف stays 4 lines from ~147px to ~181px, so surplus there is dead space while other columns suffer.
Equal or symmetric widths are wrong here because column roles and content lengths differ by an order of magnitude (53px vs 445px).
specific: "3,200 ر.س" requires 91px; at 66px the currency unit drops to its own line (r1A/r1B).
Product names need 118px (97px text) to stay on one line; 100–112px wraps two or more names (r2C, r2A/r3C, r1B).
المخزون is fixed-size: 74px covers its 53px content; 78px is harmless slack, more is waste.
الوصف never drops below 4 lines anywhere in the feasible width range, so it should simply take the remainder.

tradeoffs: One can argue for r3A (122px product) or r3B (96/78 numeric columns) as optically more generous; the cost is 4–9px taken from الوصف, which changes nothing visually but slightly weakens the 'every column at its minimum, prose takes the rest' logic. r2A/r3C trade one-lined product names for a 162px description that still needs 4 lines — a defensible but less efficient allocation.
uncertain: The exact description breakpoints are approximate: whether 145px vs 156px produces a different line count is within a few pixels, and 4–6px differences between r2B, r3A and r3B are probably imperceptible to readers. Whether a two-line product name is a real fault or acceptable breathing room is a matter of house style.

critique.good: Product names and all four headers stay on one line; price and stock remain compact, adjacent, and easy to compare; no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The description is a narrow ragged strip: long descriptions take 4 lines, making rows 1 and 3 very tall while rows 2 and 4 stay short. This creates an awkward tall-short-tall-short rhythm and leaves large empty vertical space under the product, price, and stock cells in the tall rows.
critique.cause: Widths [118,91,74,156] give the description only 135px of text after padding. Product, price, and stock consume their one-line minimums, leaving too little for the free-text column.

critique.good: Description gets 168px of text and long entries fit in 3 lines; row heights are more even (83/60/83/60), and the table stays about as short as r0A. Numeric columns remain intact.
critique.problems: The product column is only 64px of text, so every product name wraps to two lines, even short ones like لوحة مفاتيح. The primary identifier loses its one-line row-label quality and feels subordinate to the description.
critique.cause: Product width 85 is well below the 118px needed for one-line names. The 33px taken from product is given to description, which fixes the description but over-compresses the row labels.

critique.good: Product names all stay on one line and the product column reads comfortably; headers remain one line and the numeric group is clear.
critique.problems: The description is even narrower than in r0A, so long entries become 5 lines and rows 1 and 3 balloon to 129px. The table grows to 392px, with excessive white space in product, price, and stock, and the description reads as a vertical stack of fragments.
critique.cause: Product width 145 exceeds the 118px one-line need by 27px, and description width 129 leaves only 108px of text. The extra width is on the wrong side of the table.

critique.good: Description column at 181px is the widest, so the free text breaks into fewer lines than a naive equal-width layout; the stock column at 74px holds المخزون on one line and stock values read cleanly as a compact right-side pair with price; headers all fit on one line (0/4 wrapped), so the header band is a clean single stripe; product names in col 1 (118px) stay on one line for the shorter models, keeping rows legible as records.
critique.problems: The price column is the weak point: '3,200 ر.س' and '1,150 ر.س' break after the numeral, dropping ر.س onto a second line, so the numeric group reads as four stacked fragments rather than a column of comparable prices, and every row is forced to at least two price lines (rows 2 and 4 are 60px tall for one-line content). Rows 1 and 3 balloon to 106px because the description column, squeezed to 181px (160px of text), takes four lines — the tallest cell in the whole table and the sole driver of those row heights. The table is 368px tall for four products, which reads as an airy, uneven block: 106/60/106/60 alternation is a rhythm, not a hierarchy.
critique.cause: col 2 at 66px gives only 45px of text, below the 70px one-line width of '3,200 ر.س', so the currency unit is pushed to line 2. col 4 at 181px (160px text) is far below the 445px one-line description width, so descriptions need four lines; the 25px lost to a too-narrow price column is not recovered anywhere useful.

critique.good: The price/stock block is now visually a tight numeric cluster next to the identifier, and the description column at 187px is the widest, so the longest description drops from four lines to three; overall height falls from 368 to 322px and the row rhythm 83/60/83/60 is more even than r1A. Headers still all single-line. The compact numeric group reads clearly as 'compare these two'.
critique.problems: Two-line prices persist (66px width = 45px text), which keeps rows 2 and 4 at 60px even though their description is a single line — white space that serves no comparison purpose. Product names now wrap in col 1 (112px = 91px text, under the 97px one-line width), so 'حاسوب محمول' and 'سماعات لاسلكية' split into two lines and the identifier column loses its role as a crisp row label; the eye has to re-join two lines before it knows which product it is looking at. Descriptions still reach three lines, so the table is still dominated by the free-text column rather than by the comparison values.
critique.cause: col 1 at 112px is 6px under the 97px+padding needed for one-line names, causing name wraps. col 2 at 66px is 25px under the 91px needed for 'numeral + ر.س' on one line, causing price wraps and the 60px floor on short rows. col 4 at 187px (166px text) still needs three lines for the 445px one-line descriptions, so it stays the tallest cell.

critique.good: Product column is the widest text column after the description, and the numeric pair (price/stock) stays compact and adjacent; headers all sit on one line, no mid-word splits, and the table fills the 440px frame exactly.
critique.problems: Both two-word product names break onto a second line ('حاسوب محمول', 'سماعات لاسلكية'), so the identifier column — the one the reader lands on first in RTL — reads as fragments rather than records. Every row gets taller for no benefit, because the description still needs four lines. The description column also looks visually subordinate to the product column even though it is the only column doing real work with wrapping.
critique.cause: 112px product column leaves 91px of text, 6px short of the 97px one-line width; that 6px forces the wrap. Meanwhile 162px of description (141px text) is still under the ~149px needed to drop the long descriptions from 4 lines to 3, so the width taken from the product buys nothing.

critique.good: The cleanest of the three: 118px gives the product column exactly 97px of text, so 'حاسوب محمول', 'سماعات لاسلكية' and 'شاشة 27 بوصة' all sit on one line and each row reads as a single product record. Row rhythm is clear (tall description rows alternating with short ones), the numeric group stays tight, and the table is the shortest at 322px.
critique.problems: The product names fill their column with no slack — Arabic script at 15px nearly touches the cell padding, so the identifier column feels cramped against its rules. The description at 156px (135px text) is still 4 lines for the long entries, i.e. it carries all the height but gets the least generous measure.
critique.cause: 118px is the exact minimum for a one-line product name (97+21), so there is zero tolerance; the remaining 156px is simply what is left after the two numeric columns take their one-line minimums (91 and 74).

critique.good: Gives the description the most room and keeps the numeric group intact; short-description rows stay compact and the overall table height matches r2A without extra splits.
critique.problems: The product column is squeezed to 79px of text, so even 'شاشة 27 بوصة' breaks into 'شاشة 27' / 'بوصة' and names wrap to two lines — the model number survives but the identifier is split across lines, which is the worst outcome for scanning. The extra 18px handed to the description produces no line saving at all, so the trade is pure loss and the hierarchy inverts: a cramped key column beside an oversized detail column.
critique.cause: 100px product column is 18px below the 97px+21px one-line requirement; the description at 174px (153px text) is still short of what the longest entry needs to fall to 3 lines, so the width transfer has no payoff.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r3B.why: Rightmost product column keeps 'حاسوب محمول' and all product names on one line, and the price column is wide enough that '3,200 ر.س' stays intact. Description wraps cleanly to 3–4 lines. Slight waste: the price column carries more air than it needs while the description is the tightest cell in the table.

ref_equal.why: The description is squeezed into 5–6 short ragged lines and the product column is so narrow that 'حاسوب محمول' breaks over two lines, so rows become tall, uneven blocks and the eye cannot compare row units. Widths are misallocated against the content facts (445px description vs 97px product).

ref_auto.why: Description reads well in 3 lines and product names stay intact, but the price column is too narrow: the amount and 'ر.س' split onto separate lines in every row, weakening the numeric column's scan rhythm. Overall balanced but with one clear flaw.

r1A.why: Same price problem as C ('3,200' / 'ر.س' stacked), while the product column is given generous width that sits mostly empty; the description is pushed to 4 lines. Space is spent where content is short and withheld where it is long.

r3A.why: Best allocation: product, price ('3,200 ر.س') and stock each hold one line, the narrow stock column stays compact, and the freed width goes to the description, which wraps into tidy 3–4 line blocks with consistent right edges. Rows read as units and the numeric columns scan vertically.

r2B.why: Nearly identical to E: one-line product, price and stock cells, description given the dominant share with clean 3–4 line wraps and no orphaned words. Column hierarchy (identifier → numbers → prose) is clear and the rhythm across rows is even.

raw.unsure: A, E and F are very close in measured widths; I judged mainly by line breaks and leftover whitespace, so the ordering among them could shift. Also unsure whether the two-line price in C/D was a deliberate trade-off to widen the description.

r3A.why: Clean RTL hierarchy: product names and prices each stay on one line, the narrow stock column is sized to its header, and the leftover width goes to the description, which wraps into even 3–4 line blocks. Rows read as units and the price/number stays intact.

r2B.why: Same sound allocation as A, with the description column given a touch more room; description lines break at natural phrase boundaries while product names and '3,200 ر.س' remain unbroken. Balanced and easy to scan.

ref_equal.why: The description column is squeezed to a narrow strip (7–8 lines) while the stock column is wider than its content needs, and product names wrap onto two lines ('حاسوب / محمول'). Rows become very tall and the key text column is hardest to read.

ref_auto.why: Description gets generous width, but the price column is too narrow: '3,200' and the currency 'ر.س' split onto separate lines (also 450, 1,150, 280), breaking the number–unit pair and doubling price-row height.

r1A.why: Same defect as D: the price column cannot hold '3,200 ر.س' on one line, so every price breaks before the currency, and the description column is slightly narrower than in D for no gain.

r3B.why: Well-proportioned: description takes the remaining width and wraps cleanly, stock column is compact, product names and prices sit on single lines with visible breathing room. Consistent row rhythm across all four rows.

raw.unsure: A, B and F look nearly identical at this resolution; the few-pixel differences in description vs. product column widths are hard to verify, so the ranking among them could shift.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
